record.paper_title: Results and open problems in matchings in regular graphs
record.original_question: With mu_{k,n} = min_{B in Psi_{2n}} haf_k(B), is the uniform complete-graph matrix (1/(2n-1))A(K_{2n}) always a minimizer, so that mu_{k,n} = haf_k((1/(2n-1))A(K_{2n})) for every k = 2,...,n? The source explicitly resolves this proposed exact formula negatively for k = n and sufficiently large n.

evidence.quote: However for k = n and n big enough (6.3) is wrong as explained below.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let n be a positive integer and consider symmetric matrices of order 2n. Denote by Ψ_{2n} the set of all symmetric 2n × 2n matrices B = (b_{ij}) with nonnegative entries, zero diagonal, and all row sums equal to 1 (the set of symmetric doubly stochastic matrices with zero diagonal). For an integer 2 ≤ k ≤ n, define the k-th hafnian of B by

   haf_k(B) = (1/k!) ∑ b_{i_1 j_1} b_{i_2 j_2} ⋯ b_{i_k j_k},

where the sum runs over all ordered k-tuples of pairwise disjoint unordered pairs {i_1,j_1}, …, {i_k,j_k} ⊂ {1, …, 2n} (so haf_k(B) counts, with weights given by products of entries, the partial matchings of size k in the weighted complete graph on 2n vertices defined by B). Let

   μ_{k,n} = min_{B ∈ Ψ_{2n}} haf_k(B).

Let A(K_{2n}) denote the adjacency matrix of the complete graph K_{2n} (all off-diagonal entries 1, diagonal 0). Then (1/(2n−1)) A(K_{2n}) lies in Ψ_{2n}. Determine whether, for every integer n ≥ 2 and every k with 2 ≤ k ≤ n,

   μ_{k,n} = haf_k( (1/(2n−1)) A(K_{2n}) );

that is, whether the uniform matrix (1/(2n−1)) A(K_{2n}) is always a minimizer of haf_k over Ψ_{2n}.
artifact.status_search_result: The proposed exact formula is known to be false: for k = n and n sufficiently large, the uniform matrix (1/(2n−1)) A(K_{2n}) is not a minimizer of haf_n over Ψ_{2n}, so the equality μ_{k,n} = haf_k((1/(2n−1)) A(K_{2n})) fails. This disproof is recorded in surveys on matchings in regular graphs discussing the asymptotic matching conjecture.
